The method tackles computational costs of voxel carving by leveraging the massive parallelism of modern graphics hardware [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method tackles computational costs by leveraging the massive parallelism of modern graphics hardware. The evidence explicitly states: 'We have developed a streaming GPU-based voxel carving method, tackling the aforementioned computational costs of voxel carving in the context of the latest graphics hardware trends.' This confirms that the method addresses computational costs and is designed in the context of (leveraging) modern graphics hardware trends.
supported

The core innovation lies in the data structure and processing pipeline: instead of storing the entire volumetric grid in 3D textures, it employs a GPU-optimal two-dimensional data representation containing only surface voxels [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the innovation involves a GPU-optimal two-dimensional data representation containing only surface voxels, instead of storing the entire volumetric grid in 3D textures. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states that the method 'avoids the 3D texture inherent drawbacks... by employing only surface voxels in a GPUoptimal two-dimensional data representation.' This directly confirms every factual component of the claim.
supported

The sources describe the architectural choices (explicit volume, 2D surface-only representation, load balancing) but do not provide the implementation details required to code the method from scratch [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the method creates an 'explicit volume', uses a 'GPUoptimal two-dimensional data representation' (2D surface-only), and employs 'effective load balancing' to minimize data transfer. It also mentions 'interactive framerates' and 'computational costs', which implies a high-level description of performance and architecture rather than a step-by-step coding guide. The claim accurately reflects that these architectural choices are described while implementation details for coding from scratch are not provided.

It contrasts with previous approaches such as LiMS04, WoeKoch04, and ZacKar04, which either sacrificed interactivity for speed or relied on 3D texture representations with inherent drawbacks [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that previous approaches (LiMS04, WoeKoch04, ZacKar04) either sacrificed interactivity for speed or relied on 3D texture representations with inherent drawbacks. The evidence explicitly states: 'Unlike previous approaches [LiMS04, WoeKoch04, ZacKar04] our method doesn't sacrifice interactivity for speed... and avoids the 3D texture inherent drawbacks'. This implies that the previous approaches did sacrifice interactivity for speed and/or relied on 3D textures with drawbacks, which aligns perfectly with the claim.

A streaming GPU-based voxel carving method that creates an explicit volume, avoids 3D texture drawbacks by using only surface voxels in a GPU-optimal 2D data representation, and minimizes GPU-CPU data transfer through effective load balancing [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that the method is 'streaming GPU-based voxel carving', creates an 'explicit volume', avoids '3D texture inherent drawbacks' by using 'only surface voxels in a GPUoptimal two-dimensional data representation', and minimizes 'GPU-CPU data transfer' through 'effective load balancing'. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

It differs from its parent method, Voxel Carving, by explicitly optimizing for graphics hardware trends to maintain interactivity, and from previous approaches like [LiMS04], [WoeKoch04], and [ZacKar04] by avoiding the continuous access and dual-texture overhead inherent in 3D texture-based representations [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method differs from Voxel Carving by optimizing for graphics hardware trends to maintain interactivity, and differs from previous approaches ([LiMS04], [WoeKoch04], [ZacKar04]) by avoiding continuous access and dual-texture overhead inherent in 3D texture-based representations. The evidence explicitly confirms these points: it mentions tackling 'computational costs... in the context of the latest graphics hardware trends,' ensuring 'interactivity,' and avoiding '3D texture inherent drawbacks (continuous access, using two 3D textures simultaneously)' compared to the cited previous approaches.
